turns.content: Identify product 1 when acetic acid is treated with bromine, pyridine, acetic anhydride, and heat.
Determine product 2 after heating product 1 with ethanol and catalytic sulfuric acid, then product 3 after treatment with sodium cyanide.
Starting from product 3, explain the two deprotonation and alkylation steps with excess sodium hydride and 1,5-dibromopentane, and identify the cyclized product 4.

Number the cyclohexane ring of product 4 from the carbon bearing cyano and ester groups. Identify symmetry-related carbons and test whether the two hydrogens on each CH2 are homotopic, enantiotopic, or diastereotopic in an achiral solution with rapid chair interconversion.
Use that symmetry analysis to count the distinct cyclohexane-ring proton environments.
Identify and count the non-ring proton environments in the ethyl ester group.
Add the ring and ethyl-group counts to obtain the total number of distinct proton environments.

Check the ethyl-group assignment against its expected integrations: one OCH2 environment integrating to two protons and one CH3 environment integrating to three. Explain why it creates no additional ethyl proton environments.
Reconcile the two subtotals and recompute the total number of chemically distinct proton environments.
Check the count against molecular symmetry, rapid chair interconversion, and the absence of accidental peak overlap.
Report the structure of product 4, the ring and non-ring subtotals, and the total number of distinct 1H NMR environments.
